newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down, last-gasp speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down, last-gasp speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reversed early increases to close down 100 basis points at 22.00 percent on Thursday in what traders said was late speculation.

"There was money in the market, but players hung onto it and stepped in to buy at the last minute," a trader said, noting that many brokers took advantage of uncertainty over the U.S. House of Representatives vote on decertifying Mexico to "hide" liquidity.
Overnight Cetes rates reached a high of 23.50 percent at the open.
Traders said the market was skittish for most of the session before the U.S. House of Representatives vote.

Shortly before the close of trade, the House voted to censure Mexico's anti-drugs efforts, but agreed to ammendments to waive economic sanctions and grant 90 days' grace for U.S. President Clinton to obtain "reliable assurances of substantial progress" in Mexico's fight against drug- trafficking.
The market was also skittish about an rise in U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yields to 6.96 percent, from 6.93 percent in early trade, itself up from 6.87 percent on Wednesday.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 25 basis points at 24.85 percent.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity during the session by draining 1.545 billion pesos through three auctions.

Liquidity of 2.923 billion pesos is slated to return to the market on Friday from prior central bank participation. But traders said liquidity could come under pressure from demand for cash prior to the weekend and to meet twice-monthly wage bills.
